title: The Inode: A File's Map to Its Blocks
topic: Inodes — every file has a fixed-size record holding its metadata and a list of pointers to the disk blocks that contain its bytes; direct pointers handle small files in one hop, indirect pointers fan out to reach large files via a tree of block pointers

beats.narration: A file is bytes — but where on the disk do those bytes actually live?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
How does the file system find your bytes?

beats.narration: An inode answers that. It is a small record per file: who owns it, how big it is, when it changed — and a list of pointers to the disk blocks that hold the data.

elements.content: Inode card on the left with metadata rows: mode, owner, size, mtime
Pointer list section beneath metadata: 12 direct slots + 1 indirect slot
one fixed-size record per file

beats.narration: Want byte one thousand? Divide by the block size, look up the right pointer, and follow it. Twelve direct pointers cover small files in one hop.

elements.content: Highlight pointer slot index 4
Arrow draws from pointer 4 across to data-block 4
Data block 4 lights up amber when the arrow tip arrives
twelve direct pointers — one inode lookup reaches the bytes

beats.narration: Bigger files reach further. The thirteenth pointer is indirect — it points to a whole block of pointers. Now one inode lookup reaches thousands more blocks.

elements.content: Highlight the indirect-pointer slot at the bottom of the inode
Arrow draws from indirect slot to the indirect block
Indirect block of 1024 pointer cells fades in
Pick one cell inside the indirect block
Second arrow draws from the chosen cell to a far data block
Far data block lights up rose when the second arrow arrives
12 + 1024 = 1036 reachable blocks per inode
two hops — one to the index, one to the data

beats.narration: Small files travel one hop. Big files take a tree. Same inode, same shape — only the depth changes.

elements.content: Small file: one hop. Big file: a tree.
(real systems also stack double- and triple-indirect pointers)
